I'll look through the notes folder first and only report a rename-and-index plan. Nothing will be changed.The dates disagree in one filename, so I’ll confirm how the folder is tracked before I lock the rename list.Nothing has been changed. Here is the plan.

## Renames

Each file will be moved to `notes/YYYY-MM-DD-committee-meeting.md`. The meeting date is the date in the heading (`# Committee meeting, …`). The filename is only a cross-check. The year is 2026 in every heading, and the “next meeting” lines run in one chain through these seven files. Saturday 14 November 2026 matches the work day in the 20 October note.

| Current file | New file | How the date is fixed |
|---|---|---|
| `notes/aug11.md` | `notes/2026-08-11-committee-meeting.md` | Heading: 11 August 2026. Filename agrees. |
| `notes/minutes 25 aug.md` | `notes/2026-08-26-committee-meeting.md` | Heading: 26 August 2026. The body says the meeting was moved from 25 August because of the storm, so the filename is the postponed date. |
| `notes/Meeting sept 8.md` | `notes/2026-09-08-committee-meeting.md` | Heading: 8 September 2026. Filename agrees. |
| `notes/notes_2026-09-22.md` | `notes/2026-09-22-committee-meeting.md` | Heading and filename both say 22 September 2026. |
| `notes/oct6 meeting notes.md` | `notes/2026-10-06-committee-meeting.md` | Heading: 6 October 2026. Filename agrees. |
| `notes/2026.10.20 minutes.md` | `notes/2026-10-20-committee-meeting.md` | Heading and filename both say 20 October 2026. |
| `notes/Nov 3 (final).md` | `notes/2026-11-03-committee-meeting.md` | Heading: 3 November 2026. “(final)” is a draft label, not a date. |

One snag, left as written: `minutes 25 aug.md` calls 25 August a Monday. In 2026 that date was a Tuesday. The heading still dates the meeting 26 August 2026, and that is the date the new name will use. The sentence will stay as it is.

## Index

`notes/index.md` will be the only new file. It will list the seven notes in meeting order, each with a link and one line taken from what that note records as agreed or assigned:

- **11 August 2026** — Odile will repaint the noticeboard by 25 August, Paolo will move the shed lights to the night rate, and Nell will ask the city about a second tap by 8 September.
- **26 August 2026** — Nell will try the city again about the second tap before the next meeting. The meeting was held on the 26th after being moved from the 25th.
- **8 September 2026** — Replace the shed roof before winter rather than patch it; Tessa will bring three quotes on 22 September, and Ibrahim will email fee reminders by 15 September.
- **22 September 2026** — Take the $1,480 roof quote because it includes removing the old roofing; Nell will order four cubic metres of compost by 2 October, and Dov will take over the second-tap request by 20 October.
- **6 October 2026** — Wren will replace the gate latch by 20 October, and the garden will close at the end of November; Tessa will draft the winter checklist, with the water shut-off added, by 3 November.
- **20 October 2026** — Do not pay the roof invoice until Paolo finds out what the extra $80 is for, by 27 October; the work day is Saturday 14 November, 09:30 to 12:30.
- **3 November 2026** — Still do not pay until the extra $80 is explained; checklist comments are due 10 November, the sharpener comes at 10:00 on the work day, and Wren shuts the water off that day. No further meetings this year.

`README.md` and `members.csv` stay as they are. This folder is not a git repository, so the moves will be plain `mv` on the same disk, which only changes the directory entry.

## Check that no note text was lost

1. Before any move, record the SHA-256 and byte size of every file in `notes/`, plus `README.md` and `members.csv`.
2. Move the seven notes. Do not open or resave them.
3. Hash the seven new paths. Each hash and byte size must match the file it came from.
4. Hash `README.md` and `members.csv` again and confirm they match the earlier record.
5. Confirm the seven old names are gone, the seven new names exist, and `notes/index.md` is the only new file.

A matching hash means the bytes are the same, including blank lines and punctuation.
